answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away, because it is exactly the wording you wait years to see on your appointment letter, and it tells me the developers know the real service. 'Minister Salary' is the headline every outsider reaches for, and I have heard that joke at every dinner party. I would tap the second one out of curiosity and the first one out of recognition, and only the recognition would make me think the game might get the details right.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, clickbaity game about the million-dollar ministerial pay debate. I would expect a blunt joke about getting rich in politics, probably with outsider errors in grades and process, and not much feel for how a career actually moves. It would be fun for a minute but likely shallow.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider game about the slow grind of a civil service career, with appraisals, gradings, postings and waiting to be confirmed in a post. I would expect understated humour and accurate details. It is less obviously catchy to outsiders, but it signals that the game respects the real institution.

agent.why: Only one option on the screen, and answering straight is what I would do anyway.
agent.confused_by: COMP dropped 3 to 96 with no stated cause, and STAND keeps sliding.
agent.note: The branch chairman asking nobody to say 'safe' out loud is very believable.
agent.remember: Y37: DPM at MOH, age 62. Parliamentary Question had a single choice (A), answered straight. STAND 31, COMP 96 (-3), cause unknown. Still no PM succession.

best_moment.what: The Reshuffle: asking for the hard ministry nobody wants. It felt like something a real officer would do, and the ending card confirmed it raised my ceiling to Prime Minister.

worst_moment.what: A Parliamentary Question with a single choice. Late-game years like this and the Y35 townhall gave me nothing to decide, only a tap, while STAND and COMP dropped for causes I could not see.

skip_year.why: Third GE where I walked every block again. It was the same choice and the same result as before, with STAND down 6 and no explanation.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Recused from a tender where an ex-colleague's firm bid, and noted the director might reappear
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Never saw the director again as far as I recorded

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Town Council lift upgrading done slowly, with the contractor's cousin flagged as a possible resurfacing
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Did not resurface in my notes

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y10 disclosed everything in the background check, and kept honest and clean throughout
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Ending card says my file was clean enough to be boring, with integrity 100

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y52 asked for the hard ministry nobody wants
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Declassified: this was the year my ceiling rose to Prime Minister

answer.held_back_by: Mostly the game's own clock: I reached PM only at 62 and retired immediately. Within the fiction, my candour probably cost me standing with peers and seniors, since STAND fell from the 30s to 31 without any visible cause. I suspect that is why the succession took so long.
answer.ending_fair_why: Yes. A clean file, an honest career and a late PM felt consistent, and the declassified ceiling reveal was a good touch. The legacy line about people I trained landed. I was only annoyed that the PM promotion came as I was retiring.
answer.chase_next: I would chase an ending where I stay in the service as a Perm Sec or head of civil service and never go into politics. I want to see what the game does with the pure public service track I actually know.
answer.play_again_why: Not right now. The long middle stretch repeated the same choices, and the stat changes were opaque. I would come back after a few days, and only if the single-choice years are fixed.

tone_breaks.line: Started at Senior Director, Perm Sec at 33
tone_breaks.note: Nobody starts a junior officer career at Senior Director, and a Perm Sec at 33 would never happen. The MR3 vs MR4 grade order also looked odd to me.

tone_breaks.line: Director joked the system is a game
tone_breaks.note: This was a wink at the player. It broke the fiction for me, though it was brief.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was more about being confirmed in a post, integrity and slow trust than about pay. The salary mostly showed up as an ending number, and the ending line about the formula was the only place it really mattered.
